# beenfar_network (Resource)

A network: a VLAN and its IPv4 subnet.

Only the attributes set in the configuration are managed: the others are neither changed by Terraform nor reported as drift, so they can be managed in the beenfar UI. Destroying the resource deletes it entirely.

## Example Usage

```terraform
resource "beenfar_network" "iot" {
  name         = "iot"
  vlan_id      = 20
  subnet       = "10.0.20.1/24"
  dhcp_enabled = true
  dhcp_start   = "10.0.20.100"
  dhcp_stop    = "10.0.20.199"
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Required

- `name` (String) Display name, 1-64 bytes; unique.

### Optional

- `dhcp_enabled` (Boolean) Serve DHCP; needs `subnet`, `dhcp_start` and `dhcp_stop`.
- `dhcp_start` (String) First address of the DHCP pool.
- `dhcp_stop` (String) Last address of the DHCP pool.
- `domain_name` (String) DNS domain handed to clients.
- `subnet` (String) Gateway address and prefix length, e.g. `192.168.10.1/24`.
- `vlan_id` (Number) 802.1Q VLAN id, 1-4094, or 0 for untagged; unique when tagged.

### Read-Only

- `id` (String) Server-assigned identifier. Import uses it.

## Import

Import is supported using the following syntax:

The [`terraform import` command](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/cli/commands/import) can be used, for example:

```shell
# Import by id.
terraform import beenfar_network.example <id>
```
